reader.requirement: At --std 85, when two or more argument-1 values of FUNCTION ORD-MAX are equal and greatest (judged by the 1985 simple-condition rules: numeric by algebraic value with +0 = -0 and literal length not significant, nonnumeric by the program collating sequence with space extension of the shorter operand), the function returns the ordinal of the leftmost one. This holds for every argument form the 1989 module allows: identifiers of any usage/scale, literals, arithmetic expressions, figurative constants, group and numeric-edited (class alphanumeric) items, alphabetic mixed with alphanumeric, and ALL-subscripted tables, including OCCURS DEPENDING ON and reference modification. The witness covers numeric and alphanumeric literal ties and one padding tie only.

refuter.notes: ORD-MAX(A1 ALL "B") with A1 = "B " returns 01 (ALL literal taken at its literal length, so the values tie) while IF A1 = ALL "B" is false. §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 rule (3) gives an ALL literal not associated with a data item the length of the literal, and a function argument is a value rather than an operand compared with one item, so the reading is defensible. Whether a figurative constant is an admissible argument at all is a §1989:A.2.2 argument-rule matter, outside this RV rule.
